issue: Caption contains an internal contradiction on the subset/superset relationship between request-latency violations and TTFT violations.
evidence: Caption states 'a subset of TTFT violations' (mid-caption) but later states 'flags a superset of TTFT violations' (end of caption). Since TTFT ≤ request latency, the set of requests with request latency > 2 s is a SUPERSET of TTFT violations (requests with TTFT > 2 s), not a subset. The prose on printed p. 96 correctly says 'flags a superset of TTFT violations.' The two clauses in the same caption assert opposite set relationships for the same set.
acceptance_test: Replace 'a subset of TTFT violations' with 'a superset of TTFT violations' (or rephrase to 'includes all TTFT violations plus requests whose total latency exceeds 2 s despite TTFT ≤ 2 s') so the caption is internally consistent and matches the prose on printed p. 96.

issue: The red dashed-line label is clipped by the line and reads 'sample p9' rather than 'sample p99'.
evidence: At the top of the red dashed line at x≈1.33 s, the label text ends at the line; the final '9' is obscured. The caption and the inset text box both say 'sample p99 (interpolation) = 1.33s'.
acceptance_test: Re-render and confirm the label reads 'sample p99' with no glyph overlapped by the dashed line (e.g., move the label left or add a white background).

figure: Figure 6.2 — Request-latency distribution: the mean looks healthy and the p95 SLO is met
issue: The red annotation box that labels the sample-p99 vertical line is overlapped by the white legend box, so the on-chart label is truncated to 'sample p9' with the final '9' hidden behind the legend. A reader looking only at the plot cannot confirm the label reads 'sample p99'; the full value is recoverable only from the legend text and the body on p.96, which defeats the purpose of the in-plot label.
evidence: On the rendered page the red box sitting above the red dash-dot line at x≈1.33 s displays 'sample p9'; its right border and trailing character are covered by the white legend box ('mean = 0.85s / sample p99 (interpolation) = 1.33s / population p99 = 5.0 s / SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'). The two boxes occupy the same top horizontal band of the plot, so the legend is drawn on top of the red label.
acceptance_test: Reposition the legend box (or the red label) so the complete string 'sample p99' is visible with no glyph covered; re-render at 150 dpi and confirm (a) the red box's right border and all characters are unobscured, (b) the red dash-dot line at 1.33 s is still unambiguously associated with its label, and (c) the green p50/p90/p95 boxes and the 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)' box remain legible and non-overlapping.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 (Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail)
issue: The hatched '1% stragglers' region is drawn with a height comparable to the main mode (visually on the order of the tallest histogram bars, ~2000-3000 requests) rather than 1% of the stated 10,000-request population (= 100 requests, ~3% of the 3000-count axis). As drawn, the figure asserts that the straggler cluster is nearly as populous as the healthy body, which is the opposite of the caption's and prose's claim.
evidence: Caption: 'a synthetic stream of 99% log-normal requests around 0.8 s plus 1% at 5 s'; 'the darker hatched band marks the 1% straggler cluster inside it'. Prose (printed p. 96): 'the population p99 of 10,000 requests — 99% at 0.8 s and 1% at 5.0 s'. 1% of 10,000 = 100 requests; on a 0-3000 'Request count' axis that is ~3.3% of the plot height. The rendered hatched block occupies a large fraction of the plot height, and the annotation '1% stragglers > 5 s (cross the SLO)' is placed inside it, which reinforces the misreading that the cluster is large.
acceptance_test: Measure the drawn height of the hatched straggler bar against the y-axis: it must equal 100 requests (1% of the 10,000-request population), i.e. ~3% of the 3000-count axis. If the intent is to shade a region rather than draw a bar, remove the count-axis implication (e.g. use a separate band annotation with no bar, or a broken/secondary axis) and state in the caption that the band is a region, not a frequency.

issue: The caption's headline claim 'the p99 SLO is met' is supported in parentheses by '(p95 = 0.99 s <= 2 s)'. The p95 value cannot establish a p99 claim; the figure's own annotation gives the relevant number, interpolated p99 = 1.33 s <= 2 s. As printed, the parenthetical is a mismatched statistic and invites the reader to believe the p99 SLO is met on the strength of the p95.
evidence: Caption: 'the mean looks healthy and the p99 SLO is met (p95 = 0.99 s <= 2 s)'. Figure annotation box: 'mean = 0.85s / p99 (interpolation) = 1.33s / population p99 = 5.0 s / SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Prose (printed p. 96) distinguishes the interpolated p99 (1.33 s) from the population p99 (5.0 s) and says the population p99 'paints a very different picture' — so the 'p99 SLO is met' claim is true only for the interpolated reading and must say so.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the parenthetical as '(interpolated p99 = 1.33 s <= 2 s; population p99 = 5.0 s > 2 s)' and confirm the caption's claim of a met p99 SLO is explicitly qualified as holding under the interpolated reading only.

issue: The caption's final caveat appears to read 'the shading marks violations of the one 1 s SLO, not a second threshold', but the SLO drawn in the figure and used everywhere else on the page is 2 s. If the printed numeral is '1 s', the caption contradicts the figure, the annotation box ('SLO 2 s'), and the caption's own earlier phrase 'the 2 s request-latency line'.
evidence: Caption (rendered at 150 dpi): '...the shading marks violations of the one 1 s SLO, not a second threshold.' Figure annotation: 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Caption earlier: '1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line'. Prose (printed p. 96): 'the p99 SLO is met' against a 2 s line. The numeral is ambiguous at 150 dpi and must be checked against the source.
acceptance_test: Read the numeral in the source caption; it must be '2 s'. If it is '1 s', correct it. Then confirm every occurrence of the SLO value on printed pp. 96-97 (prose, figure annotation, caption) reads 2 s.

issue: The in-plot label names the 2 s line a 'TTFT budget', but the caption explicitly distinguishes the request-latency SLO from TTFT ('the 2 s request-latency line — a superset of TTFT violations'). Labeling the request-latency line as a TTFT budget lets the reader conclude that the 2 s line is a TTFT threshold, which is the opposite of the caption's careful distinction and would corrupt the TTFT-vs-request-latency reasoning the chapter is building.
evidence: Figure annotation: 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Caption: '1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line — a superset of TTFT violations'. Prose (printed p. 96): 'the p99 SLO is met' and 'the population p99 paints a very different picture' — both about request latency, not TTFT.
acceptance_test: Relabel the in-plot marker 'SLO 2 s (request latency)' (or 'request-latency SLO 2 s'), and confirm no figure label on this page equates the 2 s request-latency line with a TTFT budget.

issue: The percentile markers are not unambiguously associated with their labels: a red label near the top of the plot reads as 'sample p5' (truncated/ambiguous at print size), the blue 'p95 0.99' label sits far to the left of the blue dash-dot line at ~1.33 s, and blue is used both for a percentile marker and for the 2 s SLO line. A reader cannot reliably map each dashed line to its statistic, which is the entire point of the figure.
evidence: Rendered page shows: green 'p50 0.80' with a green dashed line at ~0.80; red 'p90 0.94' with a red dashed line at ~0.94; a red label reading 'sample p5' (or 'sample p95') above a red dashed line near ~1.0; blue 'p95 0.99' at the far left; a blue dash-dot line at ~1.33 s; and a blue 'SLO 2 s' label with a blue dash-dot line at 2 s. The figure's own annotation box states p99 (interpolation) = 1.33 s, so the line at 1.33 s is the p99 marker, not p95. In grayscale, green/red/blue dashed lines of similar dash pattern are not reliably separable.
acceptance_test: Redraw with one marker per statistic, each label placed immediately adjacent to its own line, and a distinct visual treatment for the SLO line (e.g. heavy dash-dot, or a labeled arrow) that does not reuse a percentile color. Verify at 150 dpi that every dashed line has an adjacent label naming its statistic and value, and that the p95 marker is at 0.99 s and the p99 (interpolated) marker at 1.33 s.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 (in-plot label '1% stragglers > 5 s (cross the SLO)')
issue: The label says the stragglers are '> 5 s', while the prose and caption place the cluster AT 5.0 s ('a 1% straggler cluster at 5.0 s'; 'plus 1% at 5 s'). '> 5 s' implies the cluster lies beyond 5 s, which would change the population p99 and the shape of the tail.
evidence: Figure label: '1% stragglers > 5 s (cross the SLO)'. Prose (printed p. 96): 'with a 1% straggler cluster at 5.0 s'. Caption: 'plus 1% at 5 s'.
acceptance_test: Change the label to '1% stragglers at ~5 s (cross the SLO)' and confirm it matches the prose's 'at 5.0 s'.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 page layout (also applies to printed pp. 114, 120, 127)
issue: Figure pages are vertically centered, producing large empty bands above the figure title and below the caption (roughly 1 inch of dead space above the figure on printed pp. 97, 114 and 120, and roughly 1.5 inches of trailing white below the caption on printed pp. 120 and 127). The pages read as under-filled and the figure is not anchored to the top margin where the eye expects it.
evidence: Rendered pages: on printed p. 97 the running head sits at the top and the figure title begins roughly 1 inch lower; on printed p. 114 the gap is larger; on printed pp. 120 and 127 the caption ends well above the bottom margin with no following text on the page.
acceptance_test: Re-anchor figure floats to the top of the text block (or allow the following body text to flow onto the page) so that no figure page carries more than ~0.5 inch of unexplained leading whitespace above the figure title or trailing whitespace below the caption.

issue: The drawn connector direction implies the wrong mechanism: the fan lines run downward from the query-head glyphs into the K/V box, which reads as 'query heads produce the K/V head'. In GQA the causality is the reverse — one KV head is shared by (read by) a group of query heads. The subtitle's arrow ('many query heads <- few shared KV heads') points the other way, so the figure's own subtitle and geometry disagree, and a reader could infer that GQA derives KV from query heads.
evidence: Rendered figure: three groups of blue query-head squares above three orange 'K/V' boxes, with thin lines converging downward into each K/V box; subtitle 'many query heads <- few shared KV heads' (arrow pointing left/upstream). Caption: '8 query heads share one KV head' — sharing, not derivation.
acceptance_test: Redraw the connectors with arrowheads pointing from the K/V box up to the query-head group (or as a bidirectional 'shared read' bracket labelled 'shared by 8 query heads'), and confirm the subtitle arrow and the drawn arrowheads agree in direction.

figure: FIGURE 7.1 (label '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)')
issue: The figure draws three groups (plus an ellipsis) while the label asserts 'x 8 groups'. The reader cannot tell whether the canonical configuration has 8 groups (64 query heads, 8 KV heads) or whether 'x 8' refers to the heads within each group — the same '8' is doing two jobs in one label.
evidence: Rendered figure: three groups of 8 blue query-head squares, each fanning to one orange K/V box, followed by '...'. Label: '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)'. Caption: 'the load-bearing number is the n_q : n_kv ratio (8 : 1 here)'.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the label as '8 query heads : 1 KV head per group (8 groups in the canonical model; 3 shown)' or draw all 8 groups, and confirm the caption's n_q : n_kv statement is unchanged.

issue: The top row draws three solid fixed-size state boxes side by side, visually parallel to the cumulative KV row below, which can imply that recurrent state is jointly retained per token despite the note 'Successive state snapshots, not jointly retained history'.
evidence: The top row shows 'state after t1', 'state after t2', and 'state after t3' as three solid boxes in a row; the bottom row explicitly shows cumulative KV1, KV1+KV2, KV1+KV2+KV3. The caption says recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained, but the visual encoding does not distinguish the lifetimes.
acceptance_test: Revise the top row so only the latest state is visually present (e.g., ghost/fade prior states, use a single state box with update arrows, or add an explicit 'only latest retained' visual cue) and verify a reader cannot infer joint retention from the diagram alone.

issue: The caption contradicts the drawn content: it says 'snapshot 3 retains KV1+KV3', but the third KV box in the figure contains KV1, KV2 and KV3, and the caption's own next clause says the KV row is cumulative. The drawn figure is correct; the caption's parenthetical is wrong and, as written, implies KV2 is evicted — a materially different memory behavior in a chapter about state lifetime.
evidence: Figure bottom row: boxes labelled 'KV1', 'KV1 KV2', 'KV1 KV2 KV3'. Caption: 'recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained, while the KV row is cumulative (snapshot 3 retains KV1+KV3)'.
acceptance_test: Change the caption parenthetical to '(snapshot 3 retains KV1+KV2+KV3)' and confirm it is consistent with the drawn third box and with the 'cumulative' clause.

issue: The caption defines 'Arrows = token input / state flow', but the KV-history row has no arrows at all, so the cumulative growth KV1 -> KV1KV2 -> KV1KV2KV3 is conveyed only by box contents. The reader must infer the accumulation direction, and the figure's own legend does not cover the row where the memory-growth claim lives.
evidence: Caption: 'Arrows = token input / state flow; snapshots are schematic.' Rendered figure: arrows appear only in the recurrent-update row (token -> update, update -> update); the three KV boxes at the bottom are unconnected.
acceptance_test: Add left-to-right accumulation arrows between the KV boxes (or extend the caption's arrow key to state that the KV row is shown by cumulative box contents), and confirm the arrow key covers every arrowed element in the figure.

figure: FIGURE 7.3 (Quantization choices are not execution guarantees)
issue: The 'compatible dispatch' arrow fans out to three execution-path boxes (Native FP4 math, Fused dequant, Reconstruct) with solid arrowheads to all three, which can be read as 'all three run'. The caption's actual claim is that only supported combinations can load and execute — i.e. the paths are alternatives.
evidence: Rendered figure: one arrow labelled 'compatible dispatch' splitting into three solid arrows into 'Native FP4 math', 'Fused dequant', 'Reconstruct'. Caption: 'Only supported combinations can load and execute. No compatible kernel: reject; fallback is not guaranteed.'
acceptance_test: Mark the three terminal boxes as mutually exclusive alternatives (e.g. a brace or 'one of' label on the fan-out, or dashed alternative arrows) and confirm the drawing cannot be read as simultaneous execution.

issue: The figure presents 'Error-control method: AWQ / GPTQ' and 'Numerical representation: INT4 + scheme / MXFP4 / NVFP4' as two parallel, universally applicable inputs to the packed tensor, with no indication that AWQ/GPTQ are weight-only calibration methods and do not apply to KV-cache quantization. In a chapter that also covers KV quantization, this invites the reader to apply AWQ/GPTQ to KV state.
evidence: Rendered figure: two side-by-side input boxes feeding 'Packed tensor: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)'. Caption: 'quantization (calibration) method, numerical representation, packed tensors and checkpoint container describe different parts of a deployment' — no scope qualifier on the calibration method.
acceptance_test: Add a scope qualifier to the error-control box (e.g. 'AWQ / GPTQ (weight-only)') and, if KV quantization is in scope for the figure, add a separate KV path or an explicit note that calibration methods do not apply to KV state.

issue: The caption asserts 'Bar widths are proportional to bytes', but the two bars are drawn with identical total width while representing 17 B (MXFP4) and 18 B (NVFP4). The figure therefore contradicts its own stated encoding rule, and a reader who trusts the caption will read the two formats as byte-identical in overhead.
evidence: Caption: 'Bar widths are proportional to bytes.' Rendered figure: MXFP4 bar (16 B values + 1 B scale) and NVFP4 bar (8 B + 8 B + 2 B scales) span the same x-extent. The in-figure labels give the true totals: 'Local: 17 B / 32 = 0.53125 B/value = 4.25 bit/value' and 'Local: 18 B / 32 = 0.5625 B/value = 4.5 bit/value'.
acceptance_test: Either redraw the bars so total widths are proportional (17:18) and add a scale ruler, or change the caption to 'Bar segments are labeled with byte counts; total bar widths are equal for comparison' — and verify the caption's statement matches the drawing exactly.

issue: The caption clause 'and common 1D NVFP4 two (18 B per 32 values) plus a separate FP32 scale per tensor' leaves it grammatically ambiguous whether the FP32 per-tensor scale applies to NVFP4 only (as the figure states) or to both formats. MXFP4 has no FP32 global scale, so the ambiguity is substantive.
evidence: Caption: 'MXFP4 adding one local-scale byte (17 B per 32 values) and common 1D NVFP4 two (18 B per 32 values) plus a separate FP32 scale per tensor.' Figure: 'NVFP4 global FP32 scale: 4 B per tensor, not per block.' (no global-scale note on the MXFP4 row).
acceptance_test: Rewrite as '...and common 1D NVFP4 two (18 B per 32 values), plus (NVFP4 only) a separate FP32 global scale per tensor', and confirm the MXFP4 row carries no global-scale annotation.
